D021-D013_h001.question:
I’ve just turned 42 this year, and between managing the night shift at the factory and being home to my wife, things have felt… off for a few months now. I don’t know when exactly it started, but I’ve been watching what I eat pretty closely. I used to grab fries or a burger with the crew after shift, but now I can’t stand the thought—like, if I eat something fatty, I feel like I’ll just balloon up overnight. So I stick to salads, plain chicken, black coffee. I’m down near 150 now, which is pretty light for my frame, and I *know* I keep losing, but I don’t feel like stopping.

I’m not *trying* to be thin, exactly—but the idea of gaining weight scares me. Not like a panic attack or anything, just this constant hum in the back of my head. Honestly, most days I just don’t feel like eating at all. Food doesn’t interest me. I’ve lost the spark at work too—hard to focus, easy to get irritated. I love my wife, but I’ve been keeping to myself. I can’t say if it’s the mood driving the eating changes… or the other way around. I just know I don’t feel like myself.
D021-D013_h001.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h001.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h002.question:
I’ve been struggling for a few months now—maybe six? It’s hard to track. Work’s been overwhelming; we’re short-staffed, and I’m supposed to be keeping everything together, but I just feel… off. I wake up tired, even after sleeping. My wife says I’ve gotten quiet, withdrawn. We’re still living together, sharing meals—well, she eats. I don’t know, I just don’t feel hungry. I’ll take a few bites, maybe a small portion of vegetables or plain chicken, and that’s it. I tell myself I’m fine, but I’ve noticed my clothes are looser. I’ve lost some weight—steady, not sudden—but I haven’t been trying to. Or… I don’t know if I *have* been trying.  

The truth is, I get anxious around certain foods. If there’s anything fatty or sugary on the table—like dessert or even bread—I feel this immediate dread. Not disgust, exactly, but a worry that if I eat it, the weight will pile on overnight. It doesn’t make sense, I know, but the thought sticks.  

I’m not depressed, I don’t think. I just feel numb. I care about my job, my wife… but it’s like I’m watching myself from a distance. I don’t cry, I don’t rage—I just… go through the motions.
D021-D013_h002.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h002.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h003.question:
I’ve just been feeling off for a few months now—maybe six? It’s hard to say. Ever since work slowed down a bit, I notice I’m not eating like I used to. Honestly, I don’t feel like eating much at all. I used to grab sandwiches on the job, but now I skip lunch more often than not. My wife’s noticed. She says I’ve lost weight—my pants hang on me now—but I hadn’t really been weighing myself or trying to lose anything on purpose.

I guess I’ve just started avoiding certain things. Carbs, mostly. Bread, pasta, even potatoes—something about them makes me uneasy. Same with fatty foods. It’s not that I think they’re bad for me, exactly, but I get this knot in my stomach thinking about gaining weight if I eat them. I know it sounds weird—I’m not even big to begin with.

I don’t take joy in much these days, to be honest. Haven’t felt like going out, even with my wife. I just feel… heavy, inside. Not suicidal or anything, just drained. I’ll stand in front of the fridge and close it without eating. Not because I’m proud of it—just feels easier that way.
D021-D013_h003.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h003.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h004.question:
I’ve always been careful about my diet—working in theater, you’re under a microscope every night under those lights. But lately, it’s gotten harder to manage. I cut out carbs almost completely, and fats too—anything that might show on stage. I tell myself it’s for the costume fit, but some mornings on the scale, even if it goes up half a pound, I panic. I step on it three or four times, thinking I did something wrong.

I’ve lost about ten pounds over the past few months, and honestly, I didn’t plan it that way. It just happened as my appetite dropped. I’m not hungry like I used to be. Evenings are the worst—not because of food, but because I just feel… empty. I used to look forward to rehearsing, but now I have to push myself to get through lines. My husband says I’ve changed, that I cancel dinners with friends or just pick at my plate. I want to enjoy things again, but I feel stuck—like I’m watching my life from far away.
D021-D013_h004.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h004.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h005.question:
I’ve been kind of stuck in this loop lately—I don’t really feel hungry, so I just… skip meals. Usually breakfast and lunch. I’ll tell myself I’ll eat later, but by then I don’t feel like it. It’s not that I’m trying to lose weight on purpose, but I’ve noticed my jeans are looser, and I was lighter on the scale at my last check-up. I actually check it every morning now, not because I care that much, but I guess I get weirdly tense if it goes up even half a pound. I don’t know, it just makes me feel off.

Work’s been nonstop—coding, meetings, burning the midnight oil. I don’t have much motivation outside of that anymore. I used to meet friends on weekends, but now I just stay in. I don’t feel sad exactly, but everything feels… muffled. Like I’m watching life from behind glass. I sleep a lot but still wake up exhausted. I don’t know if it’s stress or if something’s actually wrong. I’m not terrified of gaining weight or anything—I just haven’t made food a priority. And honestly, I don’t know if any of this is even worth mentioning.
D021-D013_h005.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Generalized Anxiety Disorder
D021-D013_h005.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h006.question:
I’ve been meaning to come in for a while, but between early call times and back-to-back segments, it’s hard to find the time. Lately, I just don’t feel like eating—breakfast gets skipped because I’m rushing to the studio, and by lunch, I’m not hungry. If I’m on camera, even a light salad feels like too much. I’ve lost a few pounds, and my producer mentioned I look “sharp on air,” but honestly, I’d like to lose a bit more. My clothes fit better now, though I know my team keeps side-eyeing me when I turn down meals on set.

I’ve felt dizzy a few times during live shots, and my hair’s been thinning—my stylist noticed, but I just brush it off. I haven’t had my period in a few months, but I assumed it was stress. Sleep’s been off—getting to bed late, waking up exhausted. I don’t feel joy in things the way I used to—my dog, my favorite restaurants—even going out feels pointless. Some days, I wonder if it’s all worth it. But is it depression? Or just… life? I don’t fear gaining weight, exactly—I just don’t think about it. It’s more that nothing seems to matter enough to fix.
D021-D013_h006.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D013_h006.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h007.question:
I’ve just turned 43, and honestly, things have been… off for a while. Work’s been relentless—long hours consulting for clients, a lot of screen time, not much routine. I don’t know when it started, but eating just doesn’t feel necessary anymore. I’ll have a few bites at dinner, maybe some toast in the morning, but my appetite’s nearly gone. I’ve lost weight—my clothes hang loose, and people notice. My ex mentioned it last month when I saw my daughter, but I brushed her off. She overreacts, like the doctors did. They keep asking if I’m eating enough, if I’m *trying* to lose weight. I’m not *trying*, exactly. I just… don’t feel hungry.

I don’t feel much of anything, really. Getting out of bed takes effort. I used to care about my appearance, my work—but now, it’s hard to care. I sleep too much or not at all. I know I should eat more, but food feels like a chore. I don’t fear gaining weight—honestly, I’d prefer not to keep losing. But nothing seems worth fixing.
D021-D013_h007.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D013_h007.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h008.question:
I’ve been living alone since my wife passed five years ago, and the kids come by every now and then, but mostly I’m on my own. Lately, I just haven’t felt much like eating. I used to enjoy cooking for myself, but what’s the point now? I make a small bowl of oatmeal in the morning, maybe some broth at night. I’ve lost a fair bit of weight—my clothes hang off me now—but I don’t feel sick, not really. My doctor says I’m too thin, that I should eat more, but I don’t have an appetite. I don’t feel hungry like I used to.

I’ve always been a light eater, but now it’s easier to skip meals. I know I’m thinner than I should be, but I don’t feel at risk. I walk each morning, I manage on my own, so what’s the harm? I will admit, some days I feel… heavy. Like getting out of the chair takes more than it should. I don’t laugh much anymore. My daughter says I’ve changed, that I used to be more present. I just figure this is part of getting older.
D021-D013_h008.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D013_h008.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h009.question:
I’ve just turned 44, and honestly, things have been… off for a few months now. I work long shifts at the shipyard, welding and fitting metal—hard work, used to keep me solid, but lately, I don’t feel it the same way. My wife keeps mentioning I’ve gotten thinner, and she’s not wrong. I’ve skipped meals here and there—sometimes breakfast, even lunch—just didn’t feel like eating, or nothing seemed appealing. When you're on a schedule like mine, it's easy to let it slide.  

I’ve lost some weight, steady-like, and I know I should eat more, but the idea of sitting down to a full plate? It feels overwhelming. My wife pushed me to come here, saying I’ve been distant, quiet, not myself. She’s worried I’m depressed. Maybe she’s right. I don’t feel down all the time, but there's a heaviness, like the spark’s gone out.  

But no, it’s not about looking thin or being scared of gaining weight—that’s not it. The doctor last week acted like I was starving myself on purpose, like it’s some obsession. It’s not like that. I just… haven’t had the appetite, the energy. And every time someone brings it up, it just feels blown out of proportion.
D021-D013_h009.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D013_h009.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h010.question:
I’ve just been trying to keep things simple, I guess. Lately, I don’t feel like eating much—sometimes just a few bites at dinner, if that. It’s not on purpose, really. My stomach feels full fast, or maybe I just forget. I’ve lost some weight, yeah—my clothes are loose—but people keep making it a bigger deal than it is. My mom keeps asking me to eat, and the doctor mentioned something last time, but I’m fine. I’m not trying to be skinny or anything; I just don’t have an appetite.  

Work’s been slow too. I’m an assistant on a webtoon series, so I sit at a desk most days, inking panels. It’s quiet, which I used to like, but now it’s hard to focus. I don’t feel sad, exactly… just kind of empty. Some days I don’t want to open my messages or answer calls. I sleep a lot, but still wake up tired.  

When people say I look too thin, I get annoyed. Like they’re watching me. I’m not obsessed with weight—I don’t weigh myself or anything—but I don’t see why gaining it back matters so much. I just want to be left alone.
D021-D013_h010.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Schizoaffective Disorder (Bipolar Type)
D021-D013_h010.answer: C & B. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h011.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer. As a trainer, my job’s all about energy, discipline, pushing others, but lately… I can’t push myself. I don’t know why, but I just don’t feel like eating. Not out of stress, not because I’m trying to “get leaner,” but food just doesn’t appeal. I’ll have a few bites at most—one egg, a slice of toast—and that’s it. I tell myself I’ll eat more later, but I never do.  

My weight’s been dropping. Clients have noticed, asking if I’m sick. My clothes hang loose, but when I look in the mirror… I still see someone heavy. My stomach, especially—it looks bloated, distorted. I know logically I’m not, but the image won’t change.  

I’ve lost motivation. Not just for meals, but for everything. I cancel plans, skip workouts I used to love. I feel drained, flat. Some days I wonder if this is depression, but I don’t cry or feel hopeless—just numb.  

I’m not afraid of gaining weight, not really. I’m just… disconnected. Like my body isn’t mine anymore.
D021-D013_h011.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D021-D013_h011.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h012.question:
I’ve been struggling lately—just not feeling like myself. For the past few months, I’ve lost a bit of weight, not on purpose exactly, but eating has just felt harder. I teach piano full-time, mostly children, and between lessons and grading recitals, I barely notice when I skip a meal. Carbs used to be easy to eat, but now I avoid bread, pasta—just feel better when I don’t have them. It’s not that I’m afraid of gaining weight, but I do feel a little more in control when I’m lighter. To be honest, when I look in the mirror and see I’ve lost a little more, I feel… a bit proud, like I’ve done something right.  

But that pride doesn’t last. Most days, I’m exhausted. Getting out of bed takes effort. I used to love playing piano in the evenings, but now I just sit on the couch. I still teach—my students depend on me—but I feel numb, distant. Food doesn’t appeal, but I wouldn’t say I’m terrified of eating. I just don’t care much anymore. I don’t know if it’s my body or my mood—or both—that’s really causing this.
D021-D013_h012.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D021-D013_h012.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h013.question:
I’ve always been someone who likes things under control—being an admissions officer, there’s a lot of pressure to be precise, put-together. But over the past few months, I’ve just felt… off. I’m not hungry like I used to be, so I’ve ended up cutting back—some days I’m down to coffee and maybe a salad. I’ve lost some weight, yeah, and my wife keeps saying I should eat more, but I feel better this way. Lighter. I don’t know if it’s better for my health, but I do feel a bit more in control when I stick to a strict limit.

I’ve always tied how I feel about myself to how I look, and right now, seeing the number on the scale go down even a little makes me feel like I’ve done something right—like I’m managing *something*, at least. Work’s been overwhelming, and to be honest, I haven’t been enjoying much of anything lately. I’m just… going through motions. I can’t tell if the lack of appetite is because I’m not caring as much about food, or if I’m avoiding it on purpose. I don’t panic at the thought of gaining weight—I mean, I’d just prefer not to—but I can’t pinpoint why I keep doing this.
D021-D013_h013.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D021-D013_h013.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h014.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe six? It’s hard to track because my days blend together with the markets. I’m staring at screens all night, trading, checking prices, and honestly, I just haven’t had much of an appetite. When I do eat, I keep it light—salads, black coffee, maybe an egg. I don’t count calories exactly, but I know it’s not much. I’ve lost some weight, yeah—clothes are loose—but I’m not chasing that. I just… don’t crave food the way I used to.  

Looking in the mirror, I don’t feel thin. I see softness around my gut, like I still need to tighten up. My reflection never matches what people say—“You’re too skinny now.” But I know I’m not. Not yet.  

Sleep’s been hit or miss. Some nights I’m up until 4 a.m., wired. Others, I can’t get out of bed. I used to enjoy trading—the rush, the movement—but now it feels empty. Like nothing matters much. I don’t talk to friends. Don’t want to.  

I’m not scared of gaining weight. I’m not *trying* to be a certain way. I just don’t care. Even when my hands shake or I’m dizzy. I can’t find the energy to fix it.
D021-D013_h014.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D021-D013_h014.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h015.question: Lately, I just haven’t had much of an appetite. I eat a bite or two at meals—sometimes less—because that’s all that feels manageable. I’ve lost weight over the past few months, and people have noticed, but I don’t feel out of control. If anything, it feels like one of the few things I *can* manage. My job is… hard. I spend all day looking at violent content, and by the end, I just feel hollow. Food doesn’t appeal to me, and eating feels like a chore I can skip. I don’t know if it’s the weight or just everything else, but I’ve started feeling like I’m only okay when the number on the scale is low. It’s not that I’m afraid of gaining weight—I just feel more “in place” when I’m lighter. But honestly, even when I look in the mirror, it’s hard to care. Most days, I’m just tired. I sleep too much or not at all, and it’s hard to get motivated. I don’t know if this is about food, my body, or just… everything stacking up. I don’t feel like myself, but I don’t know what would even fix it.
D021-D013_h015.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Anorexia Nervosa
    D. Major Depressive Disorder
D021-D013_h015.answer: C & D. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h016.question:
I’ve just turned 74, and since my husband passed four years ago, things have slowly changed. I live alone now, and to be honest, cooking for one doesn’t feel worth the effort. I often skip breakfast—sometimes lunch too—if I’m not hungry. My daughter says I look thin, and I suppose I have lost a bit of weight, though I haven’t stepped on the scale in months. I don’t *mean* to lose weight, but when I see things like butter, cheese, or even bread, I hesitate. There’s this nagging worry that eating them might… I don’t know, tip the balance somehow. I don’t fear becoming fat the way you see on TV, but I just feel safer keeping things light.  

Lately, I’ve been tired more than usual. I don’t get dressed until noon most days, and I’ve lost interest in the garden, which used to bring me such joy. I sleep, but not well. I wake early and just lie there. I wouldn’t say I’m sad all the time, but more like… empty. I don’t cry, but I don’t smile much either. I know I should eat more, but the thought of a heavy meal makes me uneasy. I just don’t feel like myself anymore—but I can’t say exactly why.
D021-D013_h016.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D021-D013_h016.answer: B & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h017.question:
I’ve been feeling off for a few months now—maybe longer. Things at the restaurant have been overwhelming; the stress just never lets up. I used to find comfort in food, but now I don’t even want it. Honestly, I forget to eat most days. When I do, it’s just small portions—salad, clear soups, plain grilled chicken. I don’t crave anything heavy or rich.  

I’ve lost some weight, yeah, and my wife keeps telling me I look too thin. She wants me to eat more, but the idea of a big meal makes me anxious. It’s not that I’m chasing some number on the scale—it’s more like, if I eat more, I’ll feel out of control. I avoid desserts, fried stuff—anything that feels “risky.” But it’s not like I stare in the mirror terrified of getting fat or anything.  

Mostly, I just feel… empty. Tired. I don’t enjoy cooking like I used to. I show up for my shifts, but it’s automatic. I lie awake thinking about everything and nothing. My wife says I’ve pulled away, and she’s right. I just don’t know how to explain it. I don’t hate my body, but food feels like a threat now—whether it’s because of my mood or something else, I can’t tell.
D021-D013_h017.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D021-D013_h017.answer: B & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h018.question:
I’ve been struggling lately, just feeling off. As a flight attendant, my schedule is all over the place—red-eyes, time zone shifts, eating at odd hours. I guess that’s when I started paying more attention to what I eat. I cut out most carbs and fats because I read they make you retain water and feel sluggish, and honestly, I just feel better when I avoid them. I don’t know if I need to lose more weight—I’m probably thin already, maybe even a bit too much—but I keep thinking I’ll feel better once I drop a few more pounds. I weigh myself every morning, even when I’m on layovers. If the number goes up even half a pound, I get this tightness in my chest, like something’s wrong.  

Lately, I’ve been tired. Not just from work, but a deeper kind of exhaustion. Some days, getting ready feels hard. I don’t call friends much anymore. I used to love trying new restaurants in different cities, but now I just skip meals or order tea. I don’t feel sad exactly… more like disconnected. I can’t tell if the eating habits are making me feel this way—or if I’m doing them because I already feel flat. It’s all kind of tangled.
D021-D013_h018.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D021-D013_h018.answer: B & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h019.question:
I’ve just turned 68, and since retiring from government work a few years back, things have slowly changed—subtly, but enough that my wife keeps asking if I’m unwell. I don’t feel sick, exactly, but my appetite’s been off for months now. I eat maybe a few bites at dinner—sometimes just push food around the plate. Not out of dislike for the food, mind you. It’s just… I can’t bring myself to eat more. My wife worries, says I’ve lost weight, and she’s right—I’ve had to tighten my belt, and clothes hang loose.  

I won’t lie—I’ve always disliked the idea of gaining weight. Even in my fifties, I prided myself on staying trim. Now, the thought of putting weight on makes me uneasy, though I wouldn’t say it’s a fear. More like… a discomfort. I don’t track calories, but I do feel a kind of quiet relief when I eat less.  

Lately, I’ve been tired. Not exhausted, but drained, like the days blur together. I used to tinker in the garden; now I sit in my chair reading, though even the newspaper feels heavy after a few minutes. My wife says I’ve grown quiet. I just tell her I’m fine—just getting older.
D021-D013_h019.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D021-D013_h019.answer: B & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h020.question:
I’ve just turned 41 this year, and running my own restaurant—it’s been both my pride and my weight. Literally. Since the divorce talks started with my husband six months ago, I’ve noticed I’m… smaller. Not just emotionally. I don’t feel hungry like I used to. Breakfast gets skipped because I’m reviewing invoices. Lunch? I’ll taste a bite of soup during prep and call it done. Even dinner, with the late-night cleanup, I rarely sit down.  

I’ve lost about 15 pounds, maybe more—I’ve been stepping on the scale at home every morning. I don’t know why, but I check it. If it goes up even half a pound, I feel… off. Tight. Like something’s slipping. I don’t *want* to gain weight, but I’m not sure it’s fear—more like discomfort. A twitch in my chest.  

And my mood? I wouldn’t say I’m sad, exactly. Just numb. Drained. I still open the restaurant every day, still smile at customers, but inside, it’s like I’m watching myself through glass. I don’t enjoy things like I used to—food, even time with friends. But I can’t tell if that’s the stress… or something deeper. I just know I don’t want to lose more weight. But I’m not sure I care enough to stop it.
D021-D013_h020.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Anorexia Nervosa
    C. Major Depressive Disorder
    D. Acute Stress Disorder
D021-D013_h020.answer: B & C. Anorexia Nervosa & Major Depressive Disorder

D021-D013_h021.question:
I’ve just been trying to keep things light, really. I write from home most days, and when you're alone, it's easy to forget to eat—breakfast especially. I’ll have coffee and get straight into work. Lunch sometimes passes by before I notice. I don’t avoid food for any big reason, but I do feel uneasy if I eat something heavy or rich. Like, I’ll think, *This is going to show right away*, even if it’s just a slice of cake. 

Lately, I’ve felt tired. Dizzy sometimes when I stand up. My hair’s been thinning a bit, and my period hasn’t come in a few months—my doctor mentioned it, but I just figured it’s stress. I haven’t weighed myself, but clothes fit loosely, and I haven’t minded. Honestly, I thought it was just part of being burned out. 

I don’t know… I’ve been low for a while. Nothing brings me pleasure like it used to. I lie in bed thinking how pointless everything feels, but I don’t know if that’s sadness or just being exhausted from working too much. I eat when I remember. I just… don’t prioritize myself, I guess.
D021-D013_h021.options:
A. Bulimia Nervosa
    B. Delusional Disorder

D021-D013_h022.question:
I’ve been living out at the station for about eight months now—just me, the fog, and the light. It’s quiet, which I thought would help. I don’t really feel like eating most days. Breakfast gets skipped because I’m not hungry when I wake up. Lunch? Sometimes I’ll eat a cracker or two if I remember, but if I’m trimming the wick or checking the generator, it slips my mind. Dinner’s the same—just not a priority.

I keep meaning to make a proper meal, but honestly, I get anxious when I see oil or butter. I know it’s silly, but I worry if I eat anything rich, I’ll… change. Not just gain weight—though that thought scares me, too—but that things will shift somehow, and I won’t recognize myself. But I’m not losing sleep over it. I’m fine. A little thin, maybe, but I feel okay.

The last time someone mentioned my weight, I said I’m healthy. My checks with the supply barge med tech were “within range,” so it’s not dangerous.

Lately, it’s hard to care much—about food, about company, about anything, really. I used to look forward to the rare visit, now I just… wait for them to leave. I wouldn’t say I’m sad. Just absent. Like I’m fogged in.
